correctness.rationale: With ordered row identities and visible lengths, an insertion/deletion collision of two distinct input sums cannot occur: length pattern fixes which row was edited, and the other ell rows uniquely determine all ell+1. Unedited outputs have even column parity and one-substitution outputs have a single odd column. Two input sums have column distance w+(w mod 2), so their radius-one substitution balls intersect exactly when they differ in a single data column by Hamming weight 1 or 2. Each fixed-all-but-one-column section is a classical distance-three code, giving at most A_2(ell,3) times 2^{ell(n−1)}. A row-parity check in an optimal classical code attains it, and equality forces every coordinate section optimal. Independently enumerated complete SID balls and compared all pairs for ell=1..3,n=1..2, exactly matching the criterion. For ell=8 the witness of 20 words is distance-three; optimality 20 is borrowed from published code classification, not proved by local checker. Exact formula holds all ell,n>=1 but not two edits, unlabeled rows or unknown A_2 values.
